clue.text: Passionately attached to retrospective play

indicators.note: the passionate piece is fixed on after the retrospective one

parts.note: to be retrospective is to look back at the past
to act passionately is to act in anger

explanation.surface: Someone's ardent devotion to a revival production or a backward-looking drama.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOK BACK IN ANGER is John Osborne's 1956 play, the one that gave Britain the 'angry young men'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous stage drama by John Osborne, so the answer is an example of a play.

clue.text: A daughter banned from radically different musical

indicators.note: made different, so the letters of radically are rearranged
the A and the D are barred from the letters before they are shuffled

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl is excluded from a show that is utterly unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and D out of RADICALLY, leaving RICALLY, and 'different' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing or verse is song-like and melodious, so it is a near synonym of musical as an adjective.

clue.text: Moderate losing head time after time

indicators.note: the word for moderate loses its first letter, its head in a down clue

parts.note: to moderate something is to soften it

explanation.surface: Advice to tone things down, repeatedly losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens repeatedly happens frequently, which is the plain sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Poor delivery sent north welcomed by large Victorian backwater?

indicators.note: the reversed delivery is taken into the word for large, like a guest welcomed in

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word north reads it upwards, so it is turned round

parts.note: a no-ball is an illegal delivery in cricket, a bowler's poor ball

explanation.surface: A cricketer's bad ball is sent back and welcomed by a big man from the Victorian era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' is not the 19th-century era but the Australian state of Victoria, where billabongs are common; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian oxbow lake or stagnant pool, a backwater found in the state of Victoria among others.

clue.text: Smoking student taking no part in Scottish sport

indicators.note: the student drops out of the sport's letters, playing no part in it

parts.note: curling, sliding stones across ice, is a sport of Scottish origin
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A student who smokes and refuses to join in a game of curling.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoking meat or fish is one way of preserving it, and preserving food that way is called curing.

clue.text: Lacking principles — must keep time for God, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for unprincipled has to hold the time letter inside it

parts.note: someone immoral lacks moral principles

explanation.surface: An unprincipled deity must still keep time.
explanation.definitionFit: Gods are deathless beings, so a god is an example of an immortal; the 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Rod could be a larger than normal bloke, ultimately

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large

indicators.note: the last letter of bloke is taken

parts.note: its final letter, E

explanation.surface: A rod might be a fellow of more than average size.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the shaft or bar on which wheels turn, a kind of rod.

clue.text: Complacent, rising to welcome East Indian queen getting flowers

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the other pieces inside it as a host welcomes a guest
in a down clue a rising word is read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied, complacent
E is the compass abbreviation for east
a rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied person stands up to greet an Indian queen and is given a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife; 'rising' works only in a down clue, where the reversed word reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniums are common garden and pot plants grown for their bright blooms, so they are flowers.

clue.text: Conducted bag search thoroughly

parts.note: to conduct a business is to run it, past tense ran
a sack is a large bag

explanation.surface: Someone carried out a bag search very carefully, like a customs officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to go through it hunting for something, turning everything over.

clue.text: Killer dog biting large snake

indicators.note: the dog holds the letter for large in its jaws, inside its letters

parts.note: a ratter is a dog kept to kill rats
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A vicious dog bites a big snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is the informal name for a rattlesnake, the venomous American viper with a rattling tail.

clue.text: Drink and drive round

parts.note: milk is a drink
to drive a business or a machine is to run it

explanation.surface: An instruction to have a drink and then go for a spin, perhaps a warning about drink-driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' here is a regular route, not a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk run is a routine journey, originally the milkman's daily delivery round, so it is a regular circuit.

clue.text: Nothing found in vandalised ancient river repository

indicators.note: the nothing letter is discovered inside the jumbled word
something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters of ancient are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Nothing is found in a wrecked old riverside storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges ANCIENT into CNTAINE, and 'found in' puts O inside it before R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place or vessel where things are stored, which is what any container is.

clue.text: A biblical patriarch ultimately missing bovine creature

indicators.note: the patriarch's name is missing its last letter

parts.note: Noah, builder of the ark, is a patriarch in Genesis

explanation.surface: An Old Testament patriarch ends up without one of the animals for his ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The anoa is a small wild buffalo of Sulawesi, a member of the cattle family; a crossword regular.

clue.text: Class must have right to replace new landlord

indicators.note: the right letter takes the place of the new letter in the word for a class

parts.note: a lesson is a class at school

explanation.surface: A school class must accept the right to evict a new landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessor is the party who grants a lease, so a landlord letting a property is a lessor.

clue.text: Marine offering wit, anything but dry

parts.note: salt is sharp wit, as in Attic salt
water is the very opposite of dry

explanation.surface: A Royal Marine offers a joke that is anything but dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' is not a soldier but the adjective meaning of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine means of the sea, and saltwater fish or habitats are those of the sea rather than fresh water.

clue.text: Fortune belonging to woman Spooner declared bankrupt

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words he said

parts.note: a dame is a woman
luck is fortune

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner announces that a lady's fortune has gone bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortune belonging to a woman is DAME LUCK; swapping the D and the L gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old London Stock Exchange a lame duck was a member who could not pay his debts, a defaulter or bankrupt.

clue.text: International group cut down strangely typical trees

parts.note: the European Union, an international group, abbreviated to EU

indicators.note: behaving strangely, the letters of typical are rearranged

explanation.surface: An international body fells some trees in an unusual way that is somehow typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' suggests felling, but it shortens the European Union to its initials; 'strangely' then rearranges TYPICAL into CALYPTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti is a plural of eucalyptus, the Australian gum tree, so the answer names trees.

clue.text: Cob appearing from mist initially looks nervous under threat

parts.note: haze is a light mist

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.note: its first letter, L
its first letter, N
its first letter, U
its first letter, T

explanation.surface: A cob, a sturdy horse, emerges from the mist looking skittish when threatened.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a sturdy horse or a male swan, but it is also the hazelnut or cobnut, and that is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cob, short for cobnut, is a cultivated variety of hazel, so its nut is a hazelnut.

clue.text: How tidings could arrive spread restriction from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so backwards

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: News might come from the east about a restriction that is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGE + LET, read 'from the east', becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Before email and phones, urgent news was often delivered by wire as a printed message, a telegram.

clue.text: Understand I must be in before noon train

parts.note: to take a point is to understand it

indicators.note: the I has to go inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: a.m. means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone works out that they must be in before noon to catch a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb, to point a weapon at a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a gun on someone is to point it at them, which is to take aim.

clue.text: Goes wrong having a drink after court

indicators.note: the drink is placed after the court letters

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves after having a drink once out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that acts up malfunctions, and a child who acts up misbehaves; both are going wrong.

clue.text: Free cameo — finally in favourite stone

indicators.note: the freeing word and the last letter go inside the word for favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
to rid is to free

indicators.note: the last letter of cameo is taken

parts.note: its final letter, O

explanation.surface: A free cameo brooch at last goes into a favourite jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a variety of olivine, so it is a precious stone.

clue.text: Panic about carbon being in short supply

indicators.note: the word for panic is placed around the carbon symbol

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Panic over carbon becoming scarce, like a fuel crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is hard to find because there is little of it available.

clue.text: Fruit that won't ever take off?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the furry green-fleshed fruit
second meaning: the flightless New Zealand bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' sounds like undressing or a plane; it is a bird that can never fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Chinese gooseberry fruit and the flightless bird of New Zealand that never leaves the ground.

clue.text: Key singer runs, catching a non-stop flight

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: the singer holds the A inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An important singer races to catch a direct flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is not an aeroplane trip but a flight of stairs that keeps moving.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a moving staircase, a flight of steps that runs continuously without stopping.

clue.text: Everybody trusts this, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: A strange assertion that all people believe in this.
explanation.definitionFit: In music tutti is an instruction for all players to perform together, so it means all of them.

clue.text: Fruit bugs flip after losing wings

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, like a bird losing its two wings

explanation.surface: Insects in fruit flip over after their wings fall off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Current info by worker that could help fight infection

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
I is the physics symbol for electric current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Up-to-date information from a worker about how to tackle infection.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that triggers the immune system to make antibodies, which then fight infection.

clue.text: Believed sheep to be among ruminants heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west is going right to left, so reversed
the sheep goes inside the word for ruminants

parts.note: deer chew the cud, so they are ruminants
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: It was thought that a sheep travelled west in a herd of other grazing animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is a dialect word for a ram; the reversal covers the whole deer-and-sheep combination, not just the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally supposed or considered to be, so a reputed fact is one that is believed.

clue.text: Political theorist reportedly spots first line isn't fixed

indicators.note: the spots-first piece is spoken aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: marks are spots or stains; 1st, abbreviated as IST with I for the figure one

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political thinker claims that seeing spots is first, and the party line is not fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: MARKS 1ST, said aloud, is MARXIST; 'fixed' then rearranges LINE ISNT into LENINIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist-Leninist follows the communist doctrine of Marx as developed by Lenin, a body of political theory.
